minutes.headline: Assessors heard a plan to shift the MUNIS tax-bill upload to their office, put off six to nine months; no vote.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a discussion with the interim town manager, finance director and town counsel about moving the commitment upload into MUNIS onto the assessors. Board members and a visiting past state assessors' president objected and asked that any change wait for a permanent town manager. The board also discussed warrant articles (41A, 41D, 17E, 17F), signed abatements and settlements, released overlay funds, and approved minutes.

what_happened.line: Most of the meeting was a discussion of moving the tax-bill upload into MUNIS from the tax collector's office to the assessors; no vote was taken.
The interim town manager said the change in roles will wait for the software decision, six to nine months, and he will consider waiting for a permanent manager.
Board members and a visiting past state assessors' president objected, and one member said the added duty is not in the principal assessor's contract.
Warrant articles 41D, 17E and 17F stay in the warrant, while 41A, on the tax deferral interest rate, is not being pursued as an article.
The board approved an overlay release, signed Hero Act abatements and settlements, and referred a fire-abatement reversal problem to a working session.

why_it_matters: Who prepares the upload of the tax-bill commitment decides which office is accountable if bills go out wrong, and the assessors say that change should wait for a permanent town manager and a software decision.
The overlay account pays for abatements and settlements, so releases from it affect how much room is left to absorb property tax refunds without raising the rate.
watch_next: Next meeting October 16, then November 6 and November 20; the November 6 location is not set.
A working session between the finance director and the chair on the fire abatement problem, with him invited to the next meeting agenda.
